listings.archiveReason: Test ridden; Fun, not perfect. Mechanical concerns. mechanical hold rather than a confirmed major failure. Brief metallic chatter for roughly one second at cold startup, one genuine but very brief clutch slip under heavy acceleration that could not be reproduced, and an uncertain rattly/odd clutch sensation when lugging or re-engaging. The rev-limiter behavior itself seemed normal. No documented cam-chain tensioner or clutch spring cup washer inspection; very little use by the current owner. Not willing to risk metal contamination or a major internal failure without a competent pre-purchase inspection of the clutch assembly, cam-chain tensioner, oil screens and clutch slip. listings.status: Ad retrieved Oct 23, 2026; seller availability unconfirmed
listings.visitNotes:
Assessment: Interesting $4,500 option for roomy comfort and composed handling, with touring equipment. Year remains unstated in the ad; no mechanical defect inferred. Advertised: 17,000 miles, electronic suspension, Wilbers shocks, Ohlins steering damper, Russell Daylong saddle, bar backs, ABS, heated grips, Parabellum fairing/laminar lip, SW-Motech case mounts and HEX diagnostic computer.
Questions: What is the model year? How do the Wilbers shocks integrate with the advertised electronic suspension, and what rider weight were they set for? Is the Russell saddle built for a particular rider height/weight? Are the fairing, case mounts and diagnostic computer included at $4,500?

listings.name: Yamaha MT-07
listings.note: Stock exhaust, Puig screen, CRG mirror, tail tidy.
listings.status: Ad retrieved Oct 23, 2026; seller availability unconfirmed
listings.visitNotes:
Assessment: Fun-per-mph candidate with relatively low advertised mileage, but $5,750 is a budget stretch. Actual knee room and comfort need a sit/test ride given the SV650 felt small. Advertised: stock exhaust, Puig screen, aftermarket levers, CRG bar-end mirror and Hyperpack lighting/tail tidy. Ad updated Oct 22 and retrieved Oct 23, 2026.
Questions: Which Puig screen is fitted, and how is wind buffeting at helmet height? Were the lighting changes plug-and-play or was the harness cut? Are original mirrors, levers and rear fender included?

listings.name: Kawasaki Versys 650
listings.note: 25k claimed, fully serviced; familiar comfortable platform.
listings.flag: Ad description says 25k miles; odometer field says 250,000.
listings.status: Ad retrieved Oct 23, 2026; seller availability unconfirmed
listings.visitNotes:
Assessment: Affordable benchmark on the platform Skipper already enjoyed for confidence and cornering. Does not deliver the livelier-engine change being explored. MotoJava listing and dealer website both claim 25,000 miles and fully serviced; Craigslist structured odometer field says 250,000. The discrepancy is unresolved, not assumed corrected.
Questions: Please send a current odometer photo to resolve 25,000 versus 250,000 miles. What specific work is included in the advertised full service? What is the itemized out-the-door price?

listings.name: Triumph Street Triple 675R
listings.note: Second owner, 11k miles, upgraded springs, covers, sliders.
listings.status: Ad retrieved Oct 23, 2026; seller availability unconfirmed
listings.visitNotes:
Assessment: Strong private-party alternative to the SF 2014 675R, at $5,200 and lower advertised mileage. Upgrades do not by themselves establish abuse. Advertised: second owner, 11,201 miles, .95 front springs, aftermarket seat cover, levers, covers, sliders and spools. Ad says no leaks or oil consumption. Seller requests calls, not texts; cash and M1 for test ride.
Questions: What rider weight and riding style were the .95 springs chosen for, and what rear suspension setup accompanies them? Has the bike been used on track, and which protective parts or levers were fitted for that use? Is the original seat foam retained beneath the custom cover?

listings.note: 5,245 miles, Puig screen, lithium battery, case guards.
listings.status: Ad retrieved Oct 23, 2026; seller availability unconfirmed
listings.visitNotes:
Assessment: Low-advertised-mileage, lively handling candidate, but $5,499 and travel to the Bradley area make it a stretch. Street naked despite the seller calling it a dual-sport. Advertised: 5,245 miles, garaged, never down, registration March 2027, lithium battery, Puig screen/lower fairing, KTM case guards/spools/seat cowl, cover, stand and manual.
Map limitation: pin is a coarse southern-edge approximation because Bradley lies beyond the selectable base-map area; use Bradley / Bryson-Hesperia and the original listing for travel planning.
Questions: Is the asking price inclusive of the stand, manual and all listed accessories? How effective is this specific Puig screen for a taller rider? Are original passenger-seat and bodywork parts included, and are there any fueling or exhaust modifications?

listings.name: Suzuki VanVan 200 (RV200)
listings.note: Low seat, fuel injection, fat tires; 14k miles.
listings.flag: Provisional #4 for dirt confidence and value: low-seat, mild-power, approachable full-sized street-legal learner/keeper for easy trails. Prefer the existing $2,900 Concord VanVan at 2,054 advertised miles: this saves only $200 for roughly 12,000 extra miles; that is a value comparison, not evidence of a defect. KLX230S and Santa Cruz XT250 remain ahead for dirt versatility. Basic suspension and fat tires suit relaxed riding more than rough, fast terrain; assess actual fit. Screenshot shows 2019 RV200, $2,700, Mountain View, 14,000 miles and two owners. Seller calls it lightweight, comfortable and easy to ride. Remaining description is hidden; live availability not independently verified. Assume owner-held clean title, completed major maintenance and good working condition unless seller discloses otherwise.
